content.text: {"verdict":"pass","reasons":["The rule's affiliate/contractor element is genuinely unmet: the Section 2.1 and 2.2 grants run to Corio alone, no 'Affiliate' term is defined, and 2.2 is confined to 'Corio's internal business operations' — so the deviation status is correct.","The redline is the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position: a new Section 2.11 extending the Section 2 licences to Affiliates and contractors acting on Corio's behalf, with a self-contained 'AFFILIATE' definition and a responsibility-for-compliance proviso that a licensor would expect, leaving the existing grant language untouched.","The comment is accurate and consistent with the cited text — 2.1 is expressly 'perpetual and irrevocable', 2.2 is 'royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual', and the grants are nontransferable 'except in accordance with Section 14.1', supporting the statement that the term and successor-transfer elements already satisfy the playbook.","No at-will revocation language is introduced or left standing, and the scoping ('solely in connection with the Corio Services and Corio's internal business operations as permitted by this Agreement') does not undermine the requested extension; deterministic checks corroborate."]}

reasons: The rule's affiliate/contractor element is genuinely unmet: the Section 2.1 and 2.2 grants run to Corio alone, no 'Affiliate' term is defined, and 2.2 is confined to 'Corio's internal business operations' — so the deviation status is correct.

The redline is the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position: a new Section 2.11 extending the Section 2 licences to Affiliates and contractors acting on Corio's behalf, with a self-contained 'AFFILIATE' definition and a responsibility-for-compliance proviso that a licensor would expect, leaving the existing grant language untouched.

The comment is accurate and consistent with the cited text — 2.1 is expressly 'perpetual and irrevocable', 2.2 is 'royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual', and the grants are nontransferable 'except in accordance with Section 14.1', supporting the statement that the term and successor-transfer elements already satisfy the playbook.

No at-will revocation language is introduced or left standing, and the scoping ('solely in connection with the Corio Services and Corio's internal business operations as permitted by this Agreement') does not undermine the requested extension; deterministic checks corroborate.
